Moreover, this Court is not inclined to accept the reasons assigned by the petitioner for condoning this huge https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on:

6. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Post Master General and Others Vs. Living Media India Limited and another [(2012) 3 SCC 563], while dealing with the application to condone the delay in filing the appeal, has held as follows:
28.

entities.text: Post Master General and Others Vs. Living Media India Limited and another [(2012) 3 SCC 563]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Though we are conscious of the fact that in a matter of condonation of delay when there was no gross negligence or deliberate inaction or lack of bona fides, a liberal concession has to be adopted to advance substantial justice, we are of the view that in the facts and circumstances, the Department cannot take advantage of various earlier decisions.
The claim on account of impersonal machinery and inherited bureaucratic methodology of making several notes cannot be accepted in view of the modern technologies being used and available.
The law of limitation undoubtedly binds everybody, including the Government.

29.It is the right time to inform all the government bodies, their agencies and instrumentalities that unless they have reasonable and acceptable explanation for the delay and there was bona fide effort, there is no need to accept the usual explanation that the file was kept pending for several months/years due to considerable degree of procedural red https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 30/10/2025 05:22:47 pm ) in Rev.Aplw(MD)SR.No.78791 of 2025 tape in the process.
The government departments are under a special obligation to ensure that they perform their duties with diligence and commitment.
Condonation of delay is an exception and should not be used as an anticipated benefit for the government departments.
The law shelters everyone under the same light and should not be swirled for the benefit of a few.

30. Considering the fact that there was no proper explanation offered by the Department for the delay except mentioning of various dates, according to us, the Department has miserably failed to give any acceptable and cogent reasons sufficient to condone such a huge delay.
Accordingly, the appeals are liable to be dismissed on the ground of delay.
7. In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Postmaster General's case (cited supra), this Court is not inclined to entertain this delay petition.
Accordingly, this petition is dismissed and the review application is also rejected at the SR stage itself.
